//: Firestore composite indexes for UNWIND.
The reverse-index traversal is the query T0 exists to serve: given a claim,
read its dependents ordered by depth then weight, so the UI can draw the
radius filling in from the centre. That is a collection-group query over the
`dependents` subcollection and it needs a composite index; without it the
first cascade over the hub claim's 704 direct dependents fails at runtime.

Cards 0/2/3 to this same project surfaced a real, previously-undetected
gap: this file predates tower/memory.py's Memory Bank, so the composite
index tower.memory.get_case_chain needs (and warrant.ledger.mint's
precondition check depends on, transitively) was never defined here and
the live service returned FailedPrecondition on every call. The Firebase
CLI was not authenticated in the environment that found this, so it was
applied directly via `gcloud firestore indexes composite create`
(equivalent effect, different tool) -- see
evidence/firestore/deploy-2026-08-17.md for the transcript.
